messages:
leo: morning all 1 just joined eng-platform (first day!). quick question: where do I put runbook drafts and runbook templates in Notion? i opened a few pages but i'm not sure which one is the canonical team-runbook area. also i can't edit anything yet.

anya (DevEx): welcome leo :wave: the canonical location we use now is 'Knowledge Base / Engineering / Runbooks'. there is a Team Library page under Knowledge Base that holds templates and published runbooks.

leo: any direct link? searching "runbook" gives a bunch of old forks.

anya (DevEx): link: https://notion.so/redwood/Knowledge-Base-xxxxx (short). open "Team Library" -> "Runbook Templates". use the "Duplicate" or "Use as template" button to create a copy in your team space.

leo: when i hit duplicate it says "cannot duplicate". is that because i'm not in the right group?

people-ops-bot: If you see permission errors, file an access request: https://redwood.internal/access-requests and include the Notion URL. People Ops and Docs will triage within business hours.

katie (Docs Owner): hey @leo 1 i checked — you're in the SSO but not the Notion "team-editors" group. i can add you once People Ops confirms your team. @people-ops-bot please confirm eng-platform membership for leo.

people-ops-bot: Membership confirmed for leo in eng-platform.

katie (Docs Owner): i've added you to team-editors. try duplicating again.

leo: duplication succeeded, thank you! two small questions: 1) should runbooks live under /Knowledge Base/Engineering/Runbooks/<Component> or under /eng-platform/Runbooks? 2) any naming/metadata conventions?

anya (DevEx): good q. our rule of thumb: published runbooks that are cross-team or core infra go under /Knowledge Base/Engineering/Runbooks/<Component>. Team-specific drafts or working copies go under /eng-platform/Runbooks and should link to the canonical KB page when ready.

katie (Docs Owner): naming props: please add these page properties at the top: Owner (mention), Component (select), Status (Draft/Published/Archived), Last Reviewed (date), TemplateVersion (e.g. v2025.03). For titles use: <Component> - <Runbook Short Title> - (vYYYY.MM). Example: "k8s-scheduler - pod eviction - v2025.03".

leo: nice. should i ping someone for a docs review before moving to KB?

katie (Docs Owner): yes please add the tag `@docs-review` on the page and set Status to Draft. i'll pick it up (or you can DM me the link). we run a quick checklist: verifications, play-by-play steps, run commands in code blocks, rollback steps, and escalation contacts.

leo: awesome — created the page and added @docs-review. small nit: how do we include runbook commands? i prefer fenced blocks.

anya (DevEx): fenced code blocks are perfect. include command examples and expected output. e.g.:

```
kubectl -n redwood get pods --selector=app=scheduler
# expected: 3 pods in Running state
```

leo: perfect. thanks everyone, that helped a ton :tada: i'll move the draft to KB after review and tagging.

katie (Docs Owner): thanks leo, ping if you want a quick walkthrough.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: if you need page ownership transferred later, submit via https://redwood.internal/access-requests with owner and page URL.
